description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became - no EXEC PGM= anywhere reaches it, so it is never a Spring Batch job, and it is called four times by two ONLINE programs (COTRN02C L393 and L413, CORPT00C L392 and L412). LS-DATE='1582-10-14' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. ParityCase has no member able to carry a CALL parameter, so the pair is restated here verbatim and the test class holds the authoritative copy. This program opens no file - no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no SELECT, no FD, only WORKING-STORAGE at L22 and LINKAGE at L83 - and no JCL invokes it, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter; its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Arm 5 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at L128, WHEN OTHER last at L147: FC-UNSUPP-RANGE is matched at L137 and L138 moves 'Unsupp. Range  ' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15). That literal is author-padded - 'Unsupp. Range' is 13 characters and the source literal as written is 15 - so the abbreviation, its full stop and both in-literal trailing spaces are reproduced byte for byte rather than stripped and re-padded. Severity 3 and message 2513 are DECODED from the 88-level VALUE X'000309D159C3C5C5' at L66: 0x0003 is the severity, 0x09D1 is 9*256+209 = 2513, and the facility bytes C3 C5 C5 are 'CEE' in EBCDIC. They are never interpolated from the neighbouring arms, because the numbers are non-contiguous - the previous arm is 2509 and this one skips 2510, 2511 and 2512 - so a guessed 2510 would be wrong here. 2513 IS THE ONE ERROR VALUE BOTH ONLINE CALLERS DELIBERATELY ACCEPT: each tests IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD = '0000' first (COTRN02C L397, CORPT00C L396) and only then IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM NOT = '2513' (COTRN02C L400 and L420, CORPT00C L399 and L419), reading both spans through a redefined X(04) + X(11) + X(04) + X(61) view of the same 80 bytes that independently corroborates this layout. That tolerance is why WS-MSG-NO-N PIC 9(4) REDEFINES WS-MSG-NO PIC X(04) must render the four-character string '2513' at offset 15 and WS-SEVERITY-N the four-character string '0003' at offset 0 - a 513, a ' 513' or an 02513 would silently break both callers - and it is why this single arm carries TWO cases in this folder where most arms carry one: case11 reaches the same arm through a BC era rather than a below-epoch year. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 and the group move at L122, which overwrites what L107 put in WS-DATE with the two binary length bytes followed by only the first eight characters of the date; they are NOT captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible in this environment because no Language Environment CEE* intrinsic exists to call. 14 October 1582 is Lillian day 0 - the day before the 15 October 1582 epoch and one of the ten days the Gregorian reform skipped - so it precedes the supported range, which is exactly what 'unsupported range' names; case03 pins the valid side of that boundary one day later.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '1582-10-14' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
